defense_in_depth_findings.title: Release-to-state-root binding is by operator argument, not committed bytes
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Exactly-once is durably enforced per --state-root: the atomic mkdir plus attempt-start makes replay, crash-resume, and concurrent double-run at the same state root impossible. But --state-root and --output are caller-supplied, and the exact-key release schema (set(release) == expected_keys) cannot carry a state_root pin without invalidating the release executor SHA binding, so a holder of the one approved release could deliberately re-invoke --execute with a different state root and output path after a successful terminal. This requires willful violation of GO_EXECUTE_ONCE_NO_RETRY by the sole release holder; any re-run is byte-identical by full bit-determinism and consumes zero ledger, checkpoint, shard, or expert budget, and the duplicate attempt-start would truthfully claim the same fixed ATTEMPT-1 identity, making it detectable in reconciliation. Required at the future release-approval stage: pin the concrete state-root and output paths in the approval evidence or ship an enforcing release wrapper, consistent with the accepted expert-recovery release-wrapper precedent.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Concurrent race loser exits with uncaught OSError instead of FAIL_CLOSED packet
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: If two --execute invocations race past the state_root.exists() checks, os.mkdir guarantees exactly one winner; the loser raises FileExistsError, which is not an AggregateError, so it exits with a traceback (rc 1) rather than the FAIL_CLOSED JSON packet with truthful counters. Behavior is still fail-closed (the loser computes nothing, writes nothing, and cannot write a terminal into the winner's state root because begin_attempt precedes the guarded try block). Similarly _atomic_write has a small exists()-to-os.replace TOCTOU window, bounded because state-root exclusivity excludes any second executor writer. Cosmetic/robustness only.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Synthetic-mode forbidden set omits the historical direct-DPREFIX identity and package-root manifest rejection
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: Synthetic mode rejects exactly the eight protected representative OUTPUT_SHAS. It does not additionally reject the historical direct-DPREFIX output identity (6479a835...) as a declared synthetic input, nor an --output-root containing a manifest.json whose SHA equals MANIFEST_SHA (the optional part of cycle 1's R1 remediation). Consuming any protected bytes still requires declaring their true SHA (computed-equals-declared is enforced first) and requires those exact bytes to be locally present at exactly 24576 bytes; real mode and the validator both reject the historical identity outright. Residual hardening only.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Writable-alias exclusion cannot cover pre-existing foreign write descriptors (carried from RRA-C1-D4)
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: st_nlink==1 plus mode&0o222==0 cannot exclude a write-open descriptor already held by another process; kernel-level limit shared with the accepted reuse resolver, fully mitigated because EXPECTED=BEFORE=CONSUMED holds on the validated first-read bytes and the AFTER re-read on the same device/inode-checked descriptor detects tampering. No action required.
